title: Copper Sands - quickfire integration notes
content:
Quickfire capture from 2024-10-03 intro call with Copper Sands (ops + infra + ML lead):

Context:
- Customer: Copper Sands Studios (mid-sized games studio). Looking to run Redwood Private in their GCP VPC (project: cs-prod-llm).
- Primary use: in-game NPC dialog generation + moderation for user chat. Mixed latency/throughput profile: bursts during primetime.

Notes / constraints:
- Security: corp requires BYOK (HSM-backed KMS) for model keys and audit logs forwarded to their SIEM. No egress of PII; network policy must block public model telemetry.
- Network: strict egress rules, shared VPC with game infra, NAT only for updates. Need private image registry access and registry credentials rotation.
- Hardware: prefer T4-ish (budget) but want option to burst to A10/A100 fleet. Ask: can Redwood runtime do model-family fallback when dedicated SKU not available?
- Models: plan to use an Llama-based open model; they want 4-bit quantized variant for cost. Concern: output quality regressions vs float32.
- Latency targets: 95p <= 120ms for short prompts (<=64 tokens), 95p <= 600ms for longer (<=512 tokens).
- Throughput target: sustained 200 req/s during daytime; burst to 700 req/s for 3-5 min windows.
- Caching: will benefit greatly from prefix/KV caching for repeated system prompts (npc persona). Need persistence across restarts.
- Cost sensitivity: internal target to keep inference spend < $15k/month for pilot.

Gotchas / risk areas:
- Tokenization mismatch between client-side prompt builder (custom emojis) and model tokenizer -> hallucination/gibberish risk. Recommend we provide a tokenization sanity script and recommended pre-processing rules.
- KMS integration: Copper Sands uses an on-prem HSM reachable only via peered network. Need docs on Redwood Private key provider configs and expected handshake flows.
- Autoscaling: burst requirements with strict VPC egress means cold-start time could break 95p latency. Suggest pre-warmed pool + controlled burst policy.
- Telemetry: they cannot allow logs containing PII into our hosted analytics. Need config toggles to redact or disable telemetry for that workspace.

Action items (owner — due):
- Send short tokenization sanity script + example (Ravi) — 2024-10-06
- Draft KMS/HSM integration runbook (Diego) — 2024-10-10
- Create baseline performance runbook for T4 -> A10 bursts, include expected cold-start numbers (Maya) — 2024-10-09
- Prepare cost estimate spreadsheet for pilot (Ravi + Finance) — 2024-10-07
- Add a recommended fallback model policy doc (canary -> fallback smaller quantized family) and sample config — (Ravi) — 2024-10-11

Open questions to clarify on next call:
- Are stored customer conversations (chat history) allowed to be saved to their object store, or must we configure ephemeral-only caching?
- Can their infra team provide a test HSM endpoint for integration test (non-prod)?
- Do we need to support function-calling / structured output for NPC actions (yes/no)? If yes, confirm schema and a couple example messages.

Notes to self:
- Keep docs verbose on per-prompt budgeting; gaming teams often underestimate token usage from system prompt and multi-turn history.
- Provide sample A/B prompt pair showing quality delta between 4-bit quant and fp16 for a NPC persona (short script + eval rubric).

Meeting follow-up plan:
- 30-minute technical deep-dive next Wed (Ravi + Diego + infra SME). Bring: tokenization script, sample trace from small internal run, minimal KMS handshake notes.
- Offer an internal pilot (2-week) with a pre-warmed T4 pool and KV persistence on their object store; monitor 95p latency and error rates.

Scratch ideas / experiments to propose:
- Lightweight client-side emoji-to-token preprocessor to normalize user input and reduce hallucination surface.
- Small instrumented canary implementing prefix caching with TTL per NPC persona to measure hit-rate and latency savings.

End of quickfire notes.
